brief: ULTRACODE escalation dispatch — combat core round 3

escalation.trigger: EFFORT-POLICY trigger 1 — two consecutive critic rounds at 4/10

findings: THE CRITIC'S MECHANISM WAS WRONG, ITS OBSERVATION WAS RIGHT. r2 remedy said 'interpolate the socket capsule between last frame's world pose and this frame's world pose, root delta included'. That was ALREADY true: CombatBody.evaluateRig() double-buffers sockets in world space and advance() applies root motion to pos[] BEFORE evaluating the rig. Measured per frame at d=0.8: at the champion's first active frame (af=69) the enemy root is at z=0.384 and its weapon capsule spans z=[1.34,2.57] — the blade near end is 0.95 m IN FRONT of its own root, and the root travels a further 0.79 m during the active window. The blade is ahead of the target for every active frame and the attacker walks through it. The uncovered volume is the corridor the ATTACKER'S BODY sweeps, which nothing tested on either side.

FIX (S26): hitgeometry.json §body_hazard declares the trunk parts (pelvis, torso_lower, torso_upper, head). skeleton.js double-buffers every hurtbox capsule (pa/pb). resolve.js step 8b sweeps the attacker's OWN trunk capsules prev-pose -> now-pose against the target's hurtboxes, with the identical closed-form routine, ONLY on frames where A.lastRootDelta != 0. Zero root motion = no body hazard = no proximity component, so it cannot degenerate into RI-CMB04 'how we lose' #1.
MEASURED AFTER FIX (node arena, 0.1 m steps 0..4 m): chop min 0.0 max 3.6 (was 1.2/3.6); thrust 0.1/4.0 (was 1.6/4.0); combo_a 0.0/2.9 (was 1.1/2.9); combo_b 0.0/3.5. All contiguous, no interior gap.
TURTLE TEST after fix: stationary mashing player takes 234-384 of 620 at d=0.4..2.6 (was 0 at 0.8-1.1).
tools/lib/combat-node.mjs — the combat modules run headless in bare Node (no Chromium, no engine.js). Reproduces the browser reach numbers to the digit. 574 fights in ~2 s instead of ~20 min.

HAZARD: the working tree is shared with a concurrent builder; HEAD was transiently unbootable (game/src/character/derive.js missing for ~30 s). game/src/combat/{actor,moves,player}.js and engine.js are being edited by that agent.

S26 BODY HAZARD final form: the attacker's COLLISION capsule (pelvis->head bone origins, radius = the actor's declared body radius) swept prev-pose -> now-pose against the target's same capsule, only on frames where lastRootDelta != 0. Using the trunk HURTBOX radii instead left a dead ring 0.60-0.93 m wide in which a lunging player pushed a target it could not hit (measured: halberd min reach 0.00 -> 1.40 m). Same volume for push and hit = no ring, by construction.

BODY SEPARATION (RI-CMB04 A step 5 'resolve collision', unimplemented until now) runs at the TOP of the step, relieving LAST frame's overlap before THIS frame's root motion. Putting it between root motion and the sweep deletes the overlap S26 exists to detect. Capped at 3.0 m/s ('separation FORCE', RI-AI01) so it cannot outrun a lunge. Body radius 0.30 m, NOT the statblock's radius_m (0.5 = AI spacing radius; using it made the standoff 0.9 m and W1-10's dagger, max reach 0.9 m, could never touch the champion).
TURTLE after both: stationary mashing player DIES at every stand distance 0.4-2.6 m; champion survives with 511-774 of 2876. Was: player kills a 2876-HP boss in 19 s taking 0 damage.

TRANSITION SNAPS. Three separate defects, not one. (a) poses instantiated not blended -> clips.json cross_fade, 10 f, smoothstep, applied in Rig.applyCrossFade() and triggered by `anim` changing. (b) LoopClip curves that do not close, so the pose jumps at every wrap (idle 1.293 m x624) -> closeCurve() pins the terminal key to the initial key at construction. (c) YAW SNAPS, which no pose blend can fix because they move the actor's frame: enemy.js snapped yaw to the player's bearing on the attack-start frame (3.390 m of socket, 203 m/s) and the player's facing reversed 180 deg across roll-into-attack (2.493 m). Fixed by enforcing RI-CAM02 C's bounded turn ONCE, centrally, in CombatSystem.step, with the scenario `face` override the only exemption.

WORST single-frame weapon-socket displacement after all three, excluding frame 1 (rig initialisation, which is not a transition): 0.508 m SPRINT->SPRINT (root motion at 6.6 m/s + arm swing), 0.418 m champion ATK_ACTIVE (its own weapon is 1.75 m). Every state BOUNDARY is now <= 0.367 m against a declared per-frame tip travel of 0.308 m. Was 2.528 / 2.521 / 2.293 m.

PROBE BUG FOUND AND FIXED: cmb-probe.mjs `commit` compared the live move id against the literal 'light'. W1-10's roster renamed the R1 to `r1.1`, so `id !== 'light'` was true on frame 1 of the swing and EVERY cell of the RI-CMB02 M2 commitment grid read C = CANCELLED — the item's automatic-fail signature, reported for a build in which nothing was cancelled. It now reads the id off frame 1. Grid restored byte-identical to round 2's.

PARRY HAD NO RIPOSTE FOR AN ARITHMETIC REASON, not an input one. A medium shield's parry animation is 80 f@60, the PARRIED state it creates is 56 f, and the riposte window inside that state is f7-f52. A parrier still committed to its own parry recovery becomes actionable at parry-frame 80, by which time the window closed at 52. Unreachable for every shield class. FIX: a successful parry ENDS the parrier's move on the frame it connects (resolve.js, `B.endMove(); B.actionableAt = frame`). A WHIFFED parry still pays its full whiff_recovery_f. Measured after: riposted=true at press-lead 18 and 24, pressed at parried frame k=7 (the window's first frame), 584.1 damage. Was riposted=false, damage 0, in all seven cases.

cmb-poise probe m6_parry ALSO had two defects of its own: it pressed R1 from 1.60 m against a declared riposte range of 1.20 m, and it pressed before k=7 so it fired an ordinary R1 (damage 63) and recorded `riposted: false`. Both fixed; the probe now walks in and waits for the window.

cmb-poise m3_heavy no longer vacuous: it pressed one R1 every 200 frames against a poise pool that regenerates, so nothing ever staggered and `stagger_lengths_f: []` read as a pass. Now a chain at the weapon's cadence; measures [44] for greatsword and ultra-greatsword against a 64 f heavy spec — i.e. these weapons' poise damage lands in the MEDIUM band. That is a data question for RI-CMB05/W1-10, and the probe now says so instead of returning an empty list.

cmb-poise m4_hyperarmour control now LANDS (hp 524 of 620, hit_landed true, vacuous false) — that was S26's hole inside the hyperarmour instrument. It still does not DISCRIMINATE: neither case staggers, because the champion's chop does 32 poise damage against a 48 pool, so the player never staggers whether hyperarmour is working or not. The probe needs an exhausted player (poise halved) the way m3_medium already does. NOT CLOSED, and reported rather than papered over.
PARRY STAMINA measured at exactly 22 (poise.json declares 22, spend observed 22.00 on the press frame). The round-2 figure of 26 is not reproducible on this build.

RI-AI01 §A STREAM now emitted by the exemplar (`H.traceStart` alongside `H.combatTraceStart`), written as RI-CMB07-exemplar-F*-trace.jsonl. trace-stats.mjs reads it: 0 missing fields, 0 frame gaps. Was 18 missing fields and 1 frame gap, and RI-CMB07 M0 = 0 for it.

tools/harness/cmb-reach.mjs — the instrument S26 requires every combat critic to run, shipped with the build. Probes: enemy, player, turtle, rootdz. `--root-dz` overrides every attack's root translation on a COPY of the loaded data, which closes the harness gap the round-2 critic hit (it had to edit champion_hist_marked.json and restore it from backup).

STILL OPEN: player spear has interior hit-band gaps at 1.20-1.25 m and halberd at 1.15-1.30 m — the band between where the attacker's body corridor stops and where the blade starts. Both are W1-10 roster movesets. Reported by cmb-reach as an acceptance FAIL rather than hidden.

STILL OPEN: exemplar 18 of 25 banded rows in band against a floor of 20. Failing: 2 (attacks/min 20.4 vs <=17), 5 (rolls/min 13.2 vs <=13), 16/17 (the bar never reaches zero), 22 (committed ratio 0.646 vs <=0.56), 27 (punish usage 0.182 vs >=0.50), 28 (no stamina-denied inputs). Rows 2, 22 and 27 are one problem: the bot swings more often than it lands inside the enemy's recovery.
